lines.text: In this world, this is the most illegal object on Earth.
Because nobody ever invented the wheel. So everything is carried.
Your groceries. Your sofa. Your piano. Your grandpa.
Carrying is the biggest job on the planet. Half the world are porters, and the other half pays them.
And one kid was really, really tired of carrying. Every morning, the same crate. Every night, the same sore back.
So he started building. He tried a square. It did not roll.
He tried a triangle. It rolled once, and it hurt.
Attempt number forty-seven... was round.
He put four of them under a box, and moved his whole house in one trip.
A job that takes ten porters, done by one kid, before breakfast.
The porters' guild called an emergency meeting. If wheels caught on, half the world would lose their jobs.
Pianos would roll. Grandpas would roll. Nobody would ever need to be carried again.
The boss went red.
So by lunch, the guild had a price on his head.
Porters came from every street. They were strong, they were angry, and there were a lot of them.
So the kid did the only thing he could. He rolled.
Straight down the steepest hill in the city, faster than anything had ever moved.
Porters ran. Porters dove. One porter threw a sofa.
Porters can carry a piano up a mountain, but nobody can catch a wheel going downhill.
At the bottom was the guild boss's ground-floor penthouse. And its very large window.
Everything went quiet.
The boss stood up. He looked at the kid. He looked at the wheel.
And he bought it. For a bag of gold. Not to use it. To hide it.
Now he owns the only wheel on Earth, and uses it as a coffee table.
Which is why, in this world,
